chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn Suwayd, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) looked at me, and upon me were two sandals that had been wiped (mamsuhat). He took them and turned them over, then said to me, 'Do you intend to be like a Jew?' I said, 'May I be your ransom, a person gifted them to me.' He said, 'So there is no problem.'

key_terms.أَنْ تَهَوَّدَ: That you become like a Jew (refering to their specific method of wiping footwear)
key_terms.فَدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you (a term of respect and devotion)
key_terms.قَلَبَهُمَا: He turned them over (to inspect or show)
key_terms.مَمْسُوحَتَانِ: Two items that have been wiped (dry ablution of leather footwear)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on wearing leather sandals that have been wiped (mamsuh) for ritual purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of purity' (istishab al-taharah), where the Imam (AS) initially suspects the wiping indicates a deviation from Islamic washing norms, akin to Jewish practice, but permits it once the origin is clarified as a gift. It highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding leather footwear, distinguishing between mere surface wiping and the requirement of full washing, while emphasizing that the intent or origin of the item can influence its ritual status.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, form one of our companions, from Ali Bin Suweyd who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassanasws looked at me and upon me were sandals, both Al-Mamsouh (flat without curve before the heal). So heasws took them both and turned them, then said: ‘Do you intend to be a (like a) Jew?’ I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! But rather, these were gifted to me by a person’. Heasws, ‘So there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from certain persons of our people from ibn Suwayd who has said the following:

“Once abu al-Hassan, looked at me when I was wearing sandals which were smooth. He (the Imam) took it in his hand and turned it, then said to me, ‘Do you want to be like Jews?’ I said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, it is only what a human being has given to me as a gift.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It then is not unlawful.’”
